providers.service_territory: Largest IOU serving most of northern and central Utah including Salt Lake City, Ogden, Provo metro, and rural areas statewide
providers.notes: Utah's only investor-owned electric utility (PacifiCorp d/b/a Rocky Mountain Power). Regulated by the Utah Public Service Commission. Tariff No. 52 effective April 25, 2025. Wattsmart Business program updated July 11, 2025 and again September 21, 2026.

providers.service_territory: Provo City and portions of surrounding Utah County
providers.notes: Municipal electric utility owned and operated by Provo City Corporation. Member of Utah Associated Municipal Power Systems (UAMPS). Offers electric appliance and tool rebates plus energy efficiency programs.
Independent municipal electric utility serving Heber Valley. Operates its own commercial rebate program available to General Service customers. Not regulated by PSC.

providers.service_territory: St. George City and portions of Washington County
providers.notes: Municipal utility offering solar rebates up to $20,000 for commercial systems ($2,000/kW AC). Member of UAMPS. Offers commercial energy programs.
Municipal electric utility surrounded by Rocky Mountain Power service territory. Listed by AFDC as offering alternative fuel and EV incentives. Member of UAMPS.
Municipal utility in Davis County. No confirmed standalone commercial energy efficiency rebate program found as of 2025; offers basic utility services. Member of UAMPS.

providers.service_territory: Duchesne and Uintah counties (northeastern Utah rural areas)
providers.notes: Rural electric cooperative serving northeastern Utah. No confirmed commercial energy efficiency rebate program found as of 2025 research. Member of Tri-State G&T.

providers.service_territory: Garfield, Kane, Piute, and Wayne counties (southern Utah rural areas)
providers.notes: Rural electric cooperative serving remote southern Utah counties. No confirmed commercial energy efficiency rebate program identified as of 2025. Member of UAMPS.

programs.delivery_mechanism: Prescriptive and Express path (post-purchase for Express)
programs.stacking_rules: Cannot be combined with Prescriptive Express, Non-prescriptive Typical, or Home Energy Savings program. One incentive per measure per customer.
programs.program_notes_ai: Updated effective July 11, 2025 (Tariff Schedule 140). Express path introduced for post-purchase applications on smaller/routine lighting projects with minimal paperwork. Incentives are per-watt-reduced basis. Customers categorized into three groups by annual energy usage and peak demand. Pre-installation inspection required for non-Express path to establish energy baseline. DLC Premium listing required for LED fixtures.

programs.program_name: Wattsmart Business – Small & Medium Business Express (SMBE) (2025)
programs.delivery_mechanism: Point-of-sale credit through Trade Ally vendor
required_documents: Business size verification (via verify.wattsmartbusiness.com or phone)
programs.stacking_rules: Exclusive to verified small/medium business customers through SMBE Trade Allies only. Cannot be combined with large-customer prescriptive or custom offers.
programs.rebate_payment_method: Invoice credit (Rocky Mountain Power pays Trade Ally directly; no check to customer)
programs.program_notes_ai: Expanded from previous 'Small Business Enhanced' category to include medium-sized businesses effective July 11, 2025. Customer co-pay as little as 25%. RMP pays up to 75% of project materials and installation directly to the Trade Ally vendor. Incentive appears as a credit on the customer's invoice from the trade ally. Customers must be verified at verify.wattsmartbusiness.com or call 1-866-870-3419. Projects with existing controls are not eligible.

programs.stacking_rules: One incentive per measure per customer or owner.
programs.program_notes_ai: Covers HVAC, compressed air, commercial appliances, motors, and other non-lighting efficiency upgrades. Updated effective July 11, 2025. Incentive lists published at rockymountainpower.net. Pre-approval via Rocky Mountain Power or Wattsmart Trade Ally required before ordering equipment. Incentives capped at 75% of Energy Efficiency Project Costs.

programs.program_name: Wattsmart Business – New Construction / Major Renovation (2025)
programs.stacking_rules: Cannot be combined with standard prescriptive lighting offers. Facilities newly constructed or renovating more than just lighting use this channel.
programs.program_notes_ai: Provides cash incentives and technical expertise for new construction and major renovations. Updated effective July 11, 2025. Early engagement with Rocky Mountain Power or a Wattsmart Trade Ally required before design is finalized. Eligible for both lighting and non-lighting measures as part of a whole-building approach.

programs.stacking_rules: One incentive per measure per customer or owner.
programs.program_notes_ai: Dedicated agricultural channel to help farms and dairies improve efficiency. Covers irrigation pumps, ventilation, refrigeration, and lighting upgrades. Incentives administered under Schedule 140 (Non-Residential Energy Efficiency Program).

programs.program_name: Wattsmart Business – Demand Response / Peak Reduction (2025)
programs.stacking_rules: Can be combined with energy efficiency incentives. Incentive payments for reducing consumption during peak times.
programs.program_notes_ai: Business customers earn incentive payments for reducing energy consumption during peak demand times. Separate from energy efficiency rebates. RMP also has a Battery Storage Demand Response program for customers with onsite solar generation who allow RMP to automatically manage their battery as part of the smart grid.

programs.stacking_rules: NEIF financing can be combined with Wattsmart Business incentives/rebates.
programs.program_notes_ai: Rocky Mountain Power partners with National Energy Improvement Fund (NEIF) to help businesses pay for energy upgrades through low-interest financing. Can be used in conjunction with Wattsmart Business incentives to reduce upfront project costs.

Available to all Heber Light & Power General Service customers. Program designed to offer an incentive for any project demonstrating measurable energy savings. Specific incentive amounts and eligible measures require direct contact with Heber Light & Power. As an independent municipal utility, program details are not publicly filed with the Utah PSC.

programs.program_name: Electric Tool and Appliance Rebate Program (2025)
programs.program_notes_ai: Provo City offers rebates on electric tools and appliances when old gas-powered equipment is disposed of and replaced. Reduces emissions and air pollutants. Specific rebate amounts and covered equipment require direct contact with Provo City Power.

St. George City Power offers a $2,000/kW (AC) solar rebate capped at $20,000 for commercial systems. Residential cap is $6,000. Program details and application require direct contact with St. George City utilities.

rate_schedules.schedule_name: Schedule 23 – Small General Service Distribution Voltage
rate_schedules.description: Small commercial customers without demand metering, typically under 25 kW. Tiered energy charges by season (first 400 kWh vs. additional kWh). No demand charge.
rate_schedules.notes: Tariff No. 52, effective April 25, 2025. Energy rates are approximate based on 2025 CPI insert and price summary. Exact current rates confirmed via Utah Price Summary PDF (July 1, 2026 version also available). Summer = June–September; Winter = October–May.

rate_schedules.description: General commercial service at distribution voltage, typically 25 kW to under 1,000 kW. Includes monthly demand charge per kW of measured demand. Standard non-TOU schedule.
rate_schedules.notes: Tariff No. 52 P.S.C.U. Docket 24-035-04, effective April 25, 2025. Rate values are representative based on 2025 rate case; verify exact current figures at RMP Utah Price Summary PDF. Adjustment Schedules 91, 94, 98 apply as additional percentage adjustments.

rate_schedules.schedule_name: Schedule 6A – General Service Energy Time-of-Day Option
rate_schedules.description: Optional TOU rider for Schedule 6 eligible customers. On-peak: 6 PM–10 PM Mon–Fri (except holidays). Off-peak: all other times. Summer peak rate 26.6152¢/kWh first 50 kWh/kW; additional at 9.7456¢/kWh. Updated December 1, 2025 per Docket 25-035-T12 using AMI profile data.
rate_schedules.notes: Effective December 1, 2025 update per Docket 25-035-T12. Off-peak credit of (2.8581)¢ per kWh in summer. Winter on-peak: 23.5533¢ first block. AMI meters required; DST language removed.

rate_schedules.schedule_name: Schedule 8 – Large General Service 1,000 kW and Over Distribution Voltage
rate_schedules.description: Large commercial and industrial customers with registered demand of 1,000 kW or more. TOU periods apply: June–September on-peak 3 PM–10 PM weekdays; October–May on-peak 6 AM–9 AM and 6 PM–10 PM weekdays. Holidays are off-peak. Customer transferred to Schedule 6 if below 1,000 kW for 18 consecutive months.
rate_schedules.notes: Tariff No. 52, Docket 24-035-04, effective April 25, 2025. Holidays include New Year's Day, President's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Pioneer Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas. Rate values are representative; verify via Utah Price Summary PDF.

rate_schedules.description: High-voltage transmission service for very large commercial and industrial customers. Lower energy and demand rates than distribution-voltage schedules due to customer-owned transformation. Demand charge per kW of on-peak measured demand.
rate_schedules.notes: Tariff No. 52. Rate values are representative. Schedule 9A (TOU option) also available. Verify current rates at RMP Utah Price Summary PDF. Adjustment Schedule 98 REC Revenue Adjustment applies at -0.64% for Schedule 9.

rate_schedules.schedule_name: Schedule 9A – General Service High Voltage Energy Time-of-Day Option
rate_schedules.customer_category: Large Commercial / Industrial High Voltage TOU
rate_schedules.description: Optional TOU energy rate for high-voltage general service customers (Schedule 9 customers). Specific pricing available by calling 1-866-870-3419 or on the RMP website. Schedule 98 REC adjustment is -0.70%.
rate_schedules.notes: Tariff No. 52. Rate details not published in consumer pricing insert (CPI); available by phone or RMP website. Verify current rates at Utah Price Summary.

rate_schedules.schedule_name: Schedule 10 – Irrigation and Soil Drainage Pumping Power
rate_schedules.description: Agricultural irrigation and soil drainage pumping service. Standard energy rates plus optional TOU tier effective December 1, 2025. TOU on-peak (summer June–September): 32.0834¢/kWh; off-peak: 7.1296¢/kWh. Standard tiered: first 400 kWh summer 9.3199¢, additional 12.0130¢. Schedule 98 REC adjustment -0.42%.
rate_schedules.notes: Docket 25-035-T12, filed October 15, 2025, effective December 1, 2025. Updated on/off-peak time periods and prices based on AMI data. TOU option available per Settlement Stipulation. Standard (non-TOU) rates also shown.

rate_schedules.description: Security and outdoor area lighting billed per lamp per month. Rate not published in standard CPI insert. Adjustment Schedule 98 applies at -0.14% per lamp charge. Call 1-866-870-3419 for specific pricing.
rate_schedules.notes: Tariff No. 52. Specific pricing available by calling customer service at 1-866-870-3419 or via RMP website. Schedule 11 (Unmetered Outdoor Nighttime Lighting) and Schedule 12 (Metered Outdoor Nighttime Lighting) also exist under similar structure.

rate_schedules.schedule_name: Schedule 22 – Large General Service Transmission Voltage
rate_schedules.description: Transmission-voltage service for very large industrial customers. Lowest per-kWh and per-kW rates due to customer-owned transmission infrastructure. Schedule 98 REC adjustment -0.64%. Rate details require direct contact with RMP.
rate_schedules.notes: Tariff No. 52. Specific pricing not widely published; verify via Utah Price Summary PDF or contact RMP. Typically negotiated for very large industrial loads.

rate_schedules.description: Tariff rider governing the Wattsmart Business energy efficiency incentive program for all non-residential customers. Approved by Utah PSC Docket 25-035-T07. Establishes rules for prescriptive, express, custom, and new construction incentive pathways. Not a customer-facing energy rate; governs program mechanics and DSM cost recovery.
rate_schedules.notes: Approved per DPU recommendation June 18, 2025; effective July 11, 2025. Aligns with 2025 Budget and Savings Forecast for Wattsmart Business. Includes bill credit option allowing some customers to offset Schedule 193 (DSM Cost Adjustment) charge.

rate_schedules.description: General Service commercial rate for Heber Light & Power customers. As a municipal utility not regulated by the Utah PSC, specific rate details must be obtained directly from Heber Light & Power.
rate_schedules.notes: Rates set by Heber Light & Power governing board. Not subject to Utah PSC approval. Contact 435-654-1581 or visit heberpower.gov for current tariff schedules.

rate_schedules.description: General Service commercial rate for Provo City Power customers. As a municipal utility not regulated by the Utah PSC, rates are set by Provo City Corporation and must be obtained directly from Provo Power.
rate_schedules.notes: Member of UAMPS for wholesale power supply. Rates set by city council. Contact 801-852-6000 or provo.gov for current tariff schedules.

forms.form_notes: Initiated via wattsmartbusiness.com or contacting RMP at 1-866-870-3419. Required before starting non-Express lighting or non-lighting projects to establish energy baseline. Online portal available.

Reference document listing all current prescriptive incentive amounts for Utah, effective July 11, 2025 (v7/11/2025). Required reading to determine eligible measures and incentive levels before applying.
Required for all RMP incentive payments so that a 1099-MISC can be prepared if required following incentive payment. Customer provides tax ID. Applies to prescriptive, custom, and NCMR pathways.

Available through wattsmartbusiness.com or RMP program contact. Required for HVAC, motors, compressed air, refrigeration, and other non-lighting equipment incentives. Pre-approval required before equipment purchase.

forms.program_name: Wattsmart Business – Small & Medium Business Express (SMBE) (2025)
forms.form_notes: Customers must verify their small/medium business status before accessing SMBE offers. Can be completed online at verify.wattsmartbusiness.com or by calling 1-866-870-3419. Verification based on overall customer usage, not individual meter usage.

forms.program_name: Wattsmart Business – New Construction / Major Renovation (2025)
forms.form_notes: Early engagement required before design is finalized. Application initiated via wattsmartbusiness.com or a Wattsmart Business Trade Ally. Energy modeling documentation and construction drawings required.

forms.form_name: Utah Wattsmart Business Program Changes Summary (July 2025)
forms.form_notes: Summary of changes effective July 11, 2025 covering new lighting pathways (Express, SMBE), new construction/major renovation updates, and non-lighting incentive changes. PDF summary also available from RMP.
Application for farm and dairy efficiency projects. Contact RMP at 1-866-870-3419 or through wattsmartbusiness.com to initiate. W-9 and equipment invoices required.
Application available via Heber Light & Power's commercial rebates webpage. Contact Heber Light & Power directly at 435-654-1581 for current application form and instructions.
